page.h1: Best wireless mechanical keyboard with a number pad under $60
page.desc: Four wireless mechanical keyboards with a number pad under $60 on 2026-11-21, compared by key count, battery capacity and rated hours from each maker.
page.answer: Short answer. The best budget wireless mechanical keyboard with a number pad under $60 is the Keychron J5: full size, 108 keys, 2.4 GHz and Bluetooth, 3,750 mAh rated 300 hours backlight off. For a compact 98% numpad board, the Gamakay TK101 fits 101 keys and 4,000 mAh.

page.after:
What the differences mean

  • Keys. The Keychron J5 has 108 keys. The Attack Shark X98 has 102 (108 − 102 = 6 fewer), the Gamakay TK101 has 101 (108 − 101 = 7 fewer) and the Rosewill NEON S96 has 98 (108 − 98 = 10 fewer). All four keep the number pad.
  • Workdays per charge at 8 hours a day. Keychron J5: 300 h ÷ 8 = 37.5 workdays with the backlight off, 172 h ÷ 8 = 21.5 workdays with RGB at its lowest brightness. Attack Shark X98: 200 h ÷ 8 = 25 workdays at Attack Shark's "up to" figure, which comes with no backlight condition. Gamakay and Rosewill give capacity without hours, so there is no workdays figure for the TK101 or the S96.
  • Capacity is not runtime. Keychron rates 300 h from 3,750 mAh (3,750 ÷ 300 = 12.5 mA average draw, backlight off). Attack Shark rates 200 h from 4,000 mAh (4,000 ÷ 200 = 20 mA). With RGB on, the J5's own figure is 3,750 ÷ 172 = 21.8 mA.
  • Bluetooth is the slow mode on the J5. Keychron states 1,000 Hz on the 2.4 GHz receiver and by cable (1 ÷ 1,000 = 1 ms between reports) and 125 Hz on Bluetooth (1 ÷ 125 = 8 ms). For games, use the receiver or the cable.

The Keychron J5 is the pick, and it is not a board we link to. The board on this page that we link is the Gamakay TK101, at {after:gamakay-tk101}. It wins the compact gasket-mount segment: of the two gasket-mount boards in the table it was the lower-priced on 2026-11-21, when the Attack Shark X98 was $57.79. Gamakay's price is a Black Friday sale price; its list price is $79.99. The TK101 loses to the J5 on paperwork: Gamakay states no battery hours and no polling rate, and its box list names only the keyboard, a 1.5 m USB-C cable and a keycap puller, while the USB receiver appears in a product image.

What each size label means in keys, and the battery behind it

Percent labels do not rank these boards. Gamakay calls 101 keys "98%". Attack Shark calls 102 keys "full-size". Rosewill's S96 has 98 keys. Keychron's "100%" is 108 keys on a board 435.93 mm wide and 128.93 mm deep that weighs 1,100 g (Keychron's figures). Count the keys, then look at the product photo for the navigation keys you use (Home, End, Page Up, Page Down, Insert), because the compact layouts reach their count by closing the gaps between key blocks and trimming that cluster.

Battery claims need the same care. Only Keychron gives hours with the backlight condition attached: about 300 h off and about 172 h with RGB at lowest brightness, the 300 h labelled a lab test result. Attack Shark gives "up to 200 hours" with no condition. Gamakay (4,000 mAh) and Rosewill (3,750 mAh) give capacity alone. Womier quotes 10,000 mAh for its X98 and gives no hours in the store text we read.

Where the $60 line was drawn. Every row was at or under $60 paid on 2026-11-21. Keychron's product page showed $52.49 (regular $69.99) for SKU KJ5-H3, and Keychron's own store search listed the J5 from $44.99 the same day. The page offers an "RGB Backlight (Hot-Swappable)" version and an "RGB Backlight" version, and Keychron says hot-swap applies to the hot-swappable version only, so check which version is in your cart. Left out for being over the line: the Womier X98 ($84.99 at Womier's store), the Redragon K689 PRO ($64.99 at Redragon's store; an Amazon listing was $44.64, but Redragon's page gives no battery capacity, so it has no row), the AULA F99 ($63.99 and $71.91 on the two Amazon listings read) and Royal Kludge's wireless number-pad boards ($74.99 to $99.99 at RK's store). Dealectric does not test units: every figure here is the maker's or the listing's, read on the date shown.

Not recommended

Redragon K689 (the non-PRO Wyvern), for this question. Redragon sells two boards under the Wyvern K689 name. The K689 PRO is the tri-mode wireless one. The plain K689 ($49.99 at Redragon's store on 2026-11-21) has the same 108 keys and number pad and fits the budget, but its Amazon listing title says "Wired" and Redragon's description of it names no wireless mode. It fails the wireless half of the question.
